coverage.main: Read the twenty-page arXiv 1812.10528v4 (6 October 2022), including Sections 1-7, Tables 1-6, Appendices A/B, references and biographies. Visually checked Table 3 on p. 5, metric definitions on p. 13 and Table 6/appendices on p. 15.
coverage.supplement: Appendices A and B are included on p. 15 and were read. Checked arXiv metadata and the author-linked public resource repository; no separately linked experimental supplement located. The publisher DOI landing page was unavailable through the web tool; no inaccessible material is claimed inspected.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 1, 3 and 4 classify other papers; Table 2 defines notation; Table 5 lists dataset properties; Table 6 links other works' implementations. Sections 3/4 synthesize prior methods, Section 5 explains prior evaluation metrics, and Section 6 catalogs datasets. These are not original numerical attack-transfer results. Appendix B explicitly distinguishes the empirical study in Jin et al.'s separate survey from this work. References to transfer, black-box attacks, clean accuracy and correctly classified nodes do not establish an original transfer experiment here.

f1.evidence: No original source/target transfer experiment is located. References to clean accuracy in the literature tables are not separate clean results of this survey's own trained models.

f2.evidence: The paper describes metrics from other works, including a correctly-classified-node condition for average confidence difference. This is not a denominator rule for an original cross-model attack evaluation by this paper.

f3.evidence: The generic ASR formula summarizes prior work rather than reporting an original source-success-conditioned or unconditioned transfer rate. It is not coded no merely because its formula uses all attacks.

f4.evidence: Symbolic counts in metric definitions and dataset node/edge counts are not empirical numerators and denominators for an original transfer experiment.

f5.evidence: The paper discusses graph-specific perturbation measures but supplies no original transfer evaluation to which the survey's numerical L2/L-infinity field could be applied. This is not a claim that graph budgets are deficient.

f6.evidence: The accessible author resource is a curated bibliography with paper/code links, consistent with the survey's stated purpose. With no original cross-model attack configuration located, it is neither counted as a recomputable transfer experiment nor an artifact-release failure.

artifact_checks.result: Verified v4 date and author-linked resource repository. The cached twenty-page PDF includes both appendices; no separate experimental supplement was linked in the inspected metadata.
Publisher landing page could not be accessed through the web tool. Do not infer lack of artifacts from this access failure.

Cloned and pinned the author-linked repository. Its tracked file inventory contains README.md, a curated literature table; inspected its introductory scope and representative entries. It identifies itself as a complement to this survey and links implementations belonging to other papers. No original transfer experiment or separate experimental supplement was identified, and no listed third-party implementation was executed.

bounds_exclusion.reason: No original numerical cross-model attack rate with a matched clean baseline is reported. Symbolic ASR/MCR formulas and third-party summaries do not supply data for a per-paper misclassification bound.

limitations: Retained in the frozen corpus; non-applicability must be reported separately from ambiguous reporting and recomputability failures.
This is a non-blind evidence audit, not an independent recode. No corpus prevalence or numerical bound is computed.
